01.actor: Rami bar Hama's sister and her husband Rav Avya
01.event: Her ketubah was lost and they came before Rav Yosef
01.turn: Rav Yosef cites a lenient view; Abaye objects that the halakha follows Rabbi Meir
01.outcome: Rav Yosef tells him to go write her a new ketubah
01.summary: Rav Avya's wife lost her marriage contract and the couple came before Rav Yosef. He first cited the view that a man may live with his wife without a ketubah for a time; Abaye objected, and Rav Yosef reversed himself and told Rav Avya to write her a new one.
01.missing: Whether the new ketubah was actually written
01.reason: One real event (the lost ketubah) followed by coming before a rabbi and a ruling, which is normally not a story; but the ruling is challenged and reversed, giving some conflict and change, so it sits between and goes to borderline.

02.actor: Rabbi Yohanan, Rabbi Elazar, Reish Lakish
02.event: Rabbi Elazar refutes Rabbi Yohanan's exposition and Yohanan falls silent
02.turn: Yohanan praises Elazar as expounding like Moses; Reish Lakish deflates it: it is a baraita from Torat Kohanim
02.outcome: Yohanan went out, learned Torat Kohanim in three days and mastered it in three months
02.summary: Rabbi Yohanan was expounding when Rabbi Elazar raised an objection from a baraita and Yohanan was silenced. After Elazar left, Yohanan praised him to Reish Lakish, who pointed out that it was a baraita from Torat Kohanim. Yohanan went and learned the whole work in three days and understood it in three months.
02.reason: Beyond the dialogue there is a narrated action and change: silenced, Yohanan goes out and masters the work, a causal sequence with an outcome.

03.event: He was placed in a seat and his covering tissue was torn open
03.outcome: He fathered seven children (which R. Yehuda's side would dispute by questioning paternity)
03.summary: Rabbi Ami cites the tumtum of Biri, who was operated on and then fathered seven children, as an objection to Rabbi Yehuda; the Gemara answers that Rabbi Yehuda would question whose children they were.
03.missing: The incident is only alluded to as evidence inside a legal argument; no telling of it
03.reason: Real events with a change are mentioned, but only alluded to as evidence in the legal discussion rather than narrated, which is the R-C6 shape: borderline.

04.actor: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin (or bar Zevida); Ameimar
04.event: A visiting sage was presented with cases of a woman who had relations with a slave
04.outcome: He ruled the offspring fit (or unfit, by one version)
04.summary: Rav Gazza reported that a visiting sage ruled on cases of offspring of a slave and an unmarried or married woman; versions disagree on who it was and how he ruled, and Ameimar is reported to have ruled them fit.
04.missing: Any narrated action or change besides the visit and the ruling
04.reason: A case before a rabbi and his ruling, with transmission disputes, and no other narrated action or change: under R-C0's limit this is not a story.

05.actor: Rabbi Abba bar Zavda, Marei bar Mar, Rav Huna, Rabba son of Rav Huna
05.event: A halakhic question is sent to Rav Huna via Marei bar Mar
05.turn: Rav Huna dies before it reaches him
05.outcome: His son Rabba answers in his father's name
05.summary: Rabbi Abba bar Zavda sent Marei bar Mar to ask Rav Huna whether the halakha follows Rabbi Elazar on divorce documents. Meanwhile Rav Huna died, and his son Rabba answered with his father's tradition.
05.missing: Anything beyond sending a question and receiving an answer
05.reason: Mainly quasi-speech (sending a question, answering), but a real event intervenes, Rav Huna's death, which changes how the question is answered; mainly speech with an event is borderline.

06.event: He willed a dowry to his daughter; the cost of dowries fell
06.outcome: Rav Idi bar Avin ruled the surplus goes to the sons
06.summary: A man instructed his heirs to give his daughter a dowry; dowry prices then fell, and Rav Idi bar Avin ruled the difference belongs to the orphan sons.
06.missing: Any narrated action or change after the ruling
06.reason: A circumstance followed by a ruling, with nothing else narrated: Jeff's 2026-10-25 line makes this shape not a story.

07.actor: A woman holding a bag of documents; the heirs; Rav Nahman
07.event: The heirs claimed the deposited documents from her
07.turn: She claims she seized them during the owner's life; Rav Nahman asks for witnesses and she has none
07.outcome: He rules it a seizure after death, which is void
07.summary: A woman held a bag of documents on deposit; after the depositor died, his heirs claimed it. She said she had seized it during his lifetime for a debt; before Rav Nahman she admitted she had no witnesses, and he ruled her seizure invalid.
07.reason: There is a dispute with prior acts (deposit, claim, alleged seizure), but after she comes to court it is all dialogue and a ruling; it sits between and goes to borderline.

08.actor: A man in Eretz Yisrael in love with a woman
08.event: He suffered from love and wanted to leave the Land
08.turn: He heard the teaching about the value of being buried in the Land
08.outcome: He stayed and suffered until the day he died
08.summary: Within a letter from Rabba's brothers, Ilfa's incident is quoted: a man suffering for love of a woman sought to leave Eretz Yisrael, but when he heard this teaching he stayed and endured his suffering until he died.
08.reason: An incident embedded in the letter has a protagonist, a desire, a causal turn (hearing the teaching) and an outcome; the rest of the letter is advice and not part of it.

09.actor: An unmarried man and Rav Nahman
09.event: The man came to Rav Nahman claiming he found his bride not a virgin
09.turn: Rav Nahman infers he must have had experience with prostitutes
09.outcome: He orders him flogged with palm branches
09.summary: A bachelor came before Rav Nahman claiming he had found an open opening on his wedding night. Rav Nahman ordered him flogged, reasoning that he could only know this from prostitutes.
09.reason: Mainly speech before a rabbi with a ruling, but the ruling is a sharp punitive act with some drama; between borderline and not, so borderline.

10.event: He visited Mehoza and saw a bolt hanging and said nothing
10.missing: Any response or consequence; it is cited only as evidence in a legal argument
10.reason: A bare report of what a sage saw and did not say, cited as evidence, with nothing following: R-C5.

11.actor: A woman selling belts and a man
11.event: The man snatched a belt from her
11.turn: She demanded it back; he asked if she would be betrothed if he returned it; she took it and was silent
11.outcome: Rav Nahman ruled she is not betrothed, she merely took her own property
11.summary: A man snatched a belt from a woman selling belts. When she demanded it back, he asked whether she would be betrothed to him if he gave it; she took it silently. Rav Nahman ruled that she was not betrothed, since she was taking back her own property.
11.reason: An incident with several actions (snatching, demand, taking back) and conflict, resolved by a ruling: the cow shape of R-C0.

12.actor: The wife of Rav Yosef son of Rava; Rav Nehemya
12.event: She came before Rav Nehemya demanding sustenance
12.outcome: He apportioned both, citing Mehoza's wine-drinking custom
12.summary: The widow of Rav Yosef son of Rava came to Rav Nehemya and demanded sustenance, which he apportioned; she demanded wine too, and he apportioned it, noting that Mehoza's residents drink wine.
12.missing: Further action or consequence beyond the apportioning
12.reason: A courtroom exchange where the rabbi's apportioning is itself an act that changes something; per Jeff on Ketubot 65a this keeps it borderline rather than not.

13.event: He habitually passed through Neharde'a's half-blocked gates and said nothing
13.missing: Any one-time event or consequence; a practice cited as evidence
13.reason: A habitual practice cited as halakhic evidence, with nothing happening after: a custom that leads nowhere is not a story.

14.event: He testified that his father's house bought brine with tithe money
14.missing: Any event beyond a reported custom and a scholarly reply
14.reason: Testimony about a family practice and a legal reply: a report of a custom plus ordinary discussion, no story.

15.event: He told Rav Hana to gather ten men so he could publicize a ruling
15.reason: Pure speech cited in a legal argument, no conflict and no event.

16.event: They disagreed on liability and each jumped up and swore he heard his view from Rabbi
16.turn: Each then argued his position by reasoning, in three cases
16.outcome: No resolution; the Gemara analyzes the dispute and ends in a difficulty
16.summary: Rabbi Hiyya and Bar Kappara disputed a non-priest's liability; each leapt up and swore by the Temple service that he had heard his ruling from Rabbi, then each reasoned his case. The same happened over two more cases. The rest is the Gemara analyzing their dispute.
16.missing: Any event beyond the dramatic speech acts; an outcome
16.reason: Mainly speech, but with sharp conflict (rival oaths, jumping up), which R-C2 makes borderline; segments 8-15 are the Gemara's analysis, not part of the story.

17.actor: The Israelites and the Midianite girls
17.event: They passed the girls before the High Priest's frontplate
17.outcome: Faces that turned sallow showed fitness for intercourse
17.summary: Explaining how Israel knew which Midianite girls had been fit for intercourse, Rabbi Shimon Hasida says they passed them before the frontplate, and the faces of those fit turned sallow.
17.missing: A narrated episode; this is an exegetical answer
17.reason: An exegetical elaboration of a biblical episode, which R-S1 (2026-11-12) puts out of scope rather than in the catalogue.

18.event: He permitted (or himself performed) first intercourse on Shabbat
18.reason: A bare report of a ruling or of what a sage did, with nothing following.

19.event: Engrossed in study, he wandered beyond the Shabbat limit
19.turn: Rav Hisda tells Rav Nahman that his student is in distress
19.outcome: Rav Nahman instructs that a human partition be made so he can re-enter
19.summary: Nehemya was so absorbed in learning that he walked beyond the Shabbat limit. Rav Hisda told Rav Nahman his student was stuck, and Rav Nahman said to form a partition of people so he could come back in.
19.missing: Whether the partition was made and he re-entered
19.reason: One event followed by a ruling whose outcome is only implied, the shape Jeff ruled on 2026-10-25 as not a story rather than borderline.

20.event: Each said they need no eiruv since they eat at their master's table
20.missing: Any event beyond speech about a practice
20.reason: Statements about a practice cited to resolve a legal question; speech without conflict or event.
